edges.description: Shunt-driven pulmonary overcirculation is the route by which hemodynamically significant PDA is tied to respiratory morbidity and ventilatory status.
intermediate_mechanisms: Pulmonary overcirculation with increased lung water and reduced compliance, raising ventilatory requirement in the preterm infant.

edges.description: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia occurred six-fold more often with hemodynamically significant PDA in the cited cohort. The association is observational and the ventilatory exposure sits between the shunt and the lung disease, so the edge is curated as indirect rather than as a direct cause.
intermediate_mechanisms: Prolonged pulmonary overcirculation, mechanical ventilation and oxygen exposure in the immature lung.

edges.description: Longstanding or severe left-to-right ductal shunting can remodel the pulmonary vasculature and raise pulmonary arterial pressure. The entry's own evidence treats pulmonary hypertension partly as a confounding neonatal context rather than as a proven consequence in every patient, so the edge is deliberately indirect.

High-grade intraventricular haemorrhage rose 8.7-fold when systemic hypoperfusion and pulmonary overcirculation were both present, which is the diastolic-steal route from the shunt to the brain. The cohort reports association, so the edge is curated as indirect.
intermediate_mechanisms: Systemic hypoperfusion with unstable cerebral blood flow in the preterm germinal matrix.

edges.description: High-grade retinopathy rose 18-fold in the same severe-physiology subgroup. As with the haemorrhage edge, this is an observational association routed through systemic hypoperfusion rather than a demonstrated direct cause.
intermediate_mechanisms: Systemic hypoperfusion and fluctuating oxygen delivery to the incompletely vascularised retina.
